summary: The narrator, a fugitive, flees across rooftops and alleys after leaving a half-drunk bottle with his fingerprints and DNA at a grocery store, worrying it could link him to the deaths of Korean kids at Tresting's office and to Rio's massacre of office workers. He decides to go back for the bottles, but finds the area swarming with police, with three police cars cutting off the alley and a helicopter overhead. He weighs grenades and shooting his way out against finding a better plan, reluctant to harm law enforcement who are just doing their jobs.
one_line: A fugitive narrator, trapped in a Los Angeles alley by police cars and a helicopter, weighs the risk of leaving forensic evidence at a grocery store.
key_facts: The narrator left a half-drunk bottle of alcohol at a grocery store that carried his fingerprints and DNA.
The narrator worries the bottle could put him in the system and link him to the deaths of the Korean kids at Tresting's office.
The narrator also fears a link to Rio's massacre of the office workers.
The narrator's information was probably already in the system from the incident at Arthur's office.
The narrator decides to go back to the grocery store to grab the bottles.
When the narrator returns, the place is already swarming with cops.
Three police cars screech into the alley behind the narrator, cutting off his escape route along the ground.
A helicopter's low thrum builds steadily over the narrator's position.
The narrator slips between two dumpsters to hide from the police cars.
The narrator considers using grenades to create chaos as an escape option, which he calls Plan B.
The narrator says he has never done more than kick the odd uniform in the head while escaping from police.
The narrator notes that law enforcement have never seemed like fair game as targets to him, unless they were dicks.
The narrator is thinking of Tresting when he says he does not always go around killing people.
